**Lenses**

- correctness: clean, gpt-6.1-sol via codex

- documentation-quality: findings, gpt-6.1-sol via codex

**Findings**

- security.r1.f1 (mechanical, security, A7 / the read-only constraint: "No pin grants a tool that writes" and "A reviewer's run is therefore never able to write"): The `Bash(git diff *)` and `Bash(git log *)` grants pinned for every OpenRouter lens are not read-only: both commands accept `--output=<path>`, which writes the diff to an arbitrary file, and the prefix pattern also matches invocations with shell redirection (`git diff <a> <b> > <path>`). A seat granted these patterns can write attacker-influenced bytes to any user-writable path despite the change's stated trust boundary that a reviewer's run is never able to write.
- test-adequacy.r1.f1 (mechanical, test-adequacy, A3): The tests can accept a Codex lens using its re-review tier for a whole-artifact read. Add an independent tier assertion for architectural-fit, which declares frontier and re-review mid, across the full-read scenarios.
- documentation-quality.r1.f1 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A3): The tier tests still describe re-review pricing as a consequence of the round number. The docstring saying “Round 2 resolves the declared re_review_tier” omits the delta-scope condition, and the new test name saying OpenRouter “rereads at mid” reinforces that misreading. Full rereads retain the declared tier in every round.

## Review verdict: findings (round 1, typed-code)

Head f801613c, base 9e6bee79, claim 9k9.408-r2.

**Lenses**

- correctness: findings, gpt-6.1-sol via codex

- simplification-efficiency: findings, gpt-6.1-sol via codex
- documentation-quality: findings, gpt-6.1-sol via codex

**Findings**

- correctness.r1.f1 (mechanical, correctness, A17 — Preserve the three-attempt bound and its exhaustion guidance.): A fourth dead-run claim can bypass the exhaustion handler. It returns off-ladder, incorrectly says a failover is still accepted, omits halt guidance, and leaves the final failure unrecorded.
- correctness.r1.f2 (mechanical, correctness, A17 — A dead run on the failover seat ends the ladder and halts the round.): A dead run on the failover seat loses halt guidance when an earlier attempt returned unusable output. The dispatcher consequently receives a refusal that closes only the lens instead of halting the round.
- test-adequacy.r1.f1 (mechanical, test-adequacy, A3): No test independently pins the re-review tier for a later full read. Reverting security to frontier during a round-2 sweep could pass while dispatching the wrong model. Assert the expected tier from the roster and round number before checking its pin.
- test-adequacy.r1.f2 (mechanical, test-adequacy, A13): The doctrine evaluation uses readers with additional context, so its passing answers do not establish that the named files alone determine the dispatch. Repeat the twenty-seven scenarios with the required isolated inputs.
- simplification-efficiency.r1.f1 (mechanical, simplification-efficiency, A18: Every lens receives a unified diff file over its scope.): change_diffs recomputes and buffers the same diff separately for every lens sharing a revision pair. Reusing the computed bytes per pair would preserve every required file and refusal behavior while eliminating repeated Git work and duplicate memory.
- documentation-quality.r1.f1 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A13): The round-1 failover example uses effort high, contradicting the full-scope OpenRouter pin. A dispatcher following the example dispatches at the wrong effort.
- documentation-quality.r1.f2 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A13, A17): The doctrine says every refusal ends the lens, although an off-ladder refusal permits a corrected claim. Following this instruction abandons a recoverable lens and leaves the round incomplete.
- documentation-quality.r1.f3 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A13, A17): The empty-output guidance asserts that the reviewer never ran and directs a transport-error recovery. A watchdog-ended dead run can also leave no output, so this guidance sends the dispatcher past the required effort step-down.
- documentation-quality.r1.f4 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A13): The recovery comment still recommends another model on the same transport when one model is saturated. That rationale contradicts the pinned failover decision and suggests a free-hand model substitution.
- documentation-quality.r1.f5 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A17): The exhausted helper's docstring still limits halt guidance to transport-class failures. It misstates the helper's current behavior for dead runs.

- simplification-efficiency: clean, gpt-6.1-sol via codex
- documentation-quality: findings, gpt-6.1-sol via codex

**Findings**

- correctness.r2.f1 (mechanical, correctness, A17: A dead-run claim is accepted in exactly two forms: a lower effort on the same transport and model, or the other transport.): The gate accepts any different transport string as failover. After an initial Codex attempt, a dead-run claim with --transport openai is authorized and spends an attempt despite naming no valid failover seat. A subsequent claim for the actual OpenRouter failover is then refused as exhausted and halts the round.
- test-adequacy.r2.f1 (mechanical, test-adequacy, A17): The tests do not pin exhaustion when a dead-run claim tries to return to the starting transport after failover. A regression could return off-ladder without halt guidance, telling the dispatcher to correct and retry an exhausted lens. Parameterize the post-failover test over both requested transports.
- documentation-quality.r2.f1 (mechanical, documentation-quality, A17): The ROUTE_FAILURES comment implies that an earlier unusable output prevents the round from halting. The current rule considers each route's last failure, so a route that produced unusable output and then died can still trigger a halt.

Prior dispositions carried forward: 10 (10 fixed).
